protocol.name: cupertino_control_v1

description.summary: native scoped desktop control and trusted session consent

protocol.description: Only the compositor-created controller connection sees the manager. Binding it grants no observation, capture or input authority. Version 1 remains discovery-only. Version 2 requests explicit output-scoped consent from the private session authority. Fresh physical input on its registered surface is required to approve. Lock, disconnect and stop revoke a run. Output capture uses ext-image-copy-capture, with sources bound to the exact approved run epoch. Version 3 adds consented native semantic observation and actions, with sealed bounded publications owned by each application surface. Version 4 names the app each run comes from: the person's remembered answer for that app decides a request at once, and the session authority asks only for services the app has no answer for. Physical input never suspends a run; an authentication prompt suspends it until the prompt closes. Version 5 lets one controller connection serve several runs at once, one per local peer, each with its own epoch, held input and captures.

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection no longer holds the controller capability

entry.name: session_exists
entry.summary: the connection already has as many live sessions as allowed

entry.name: exhausted
entry.summary: the server cannot assign another unique run epoch

request.name: destroy

description.summary: release this manager

request.description: Existing session objects remain alive. This does not cancel or destroy them.

request.name: get_session

description.summary: create an inactive session

request.description: At most one session may be live for a connection, across all its manager bindings; from version 5 at most eight, created through a manager bound at version 5. Destroying one allows another session with a fresh epoch. The server immediately sends created, then status with serial zero. The manager's capability is checked again for every request. No consent or mutation is implied.

entry.name: stale_epoch
entry.summary: the request names another run epoch

entry.name: stale_geometry
entry.summary: an earlier geometry revision, or for perform an earlier publication revision

entry.name: unidentified
entry.summary: the app the run comes from cannot be named

description.summary: end this session and invalidate its epoch

request.name: query

description.summary: query the status of this exact run

request.description: serial is the caller's correlation value and must be nonzero; it is echoed unchanged in the reply. An epoch other than the one in created is refused without reporting session state. Querying has no side effect. The controller capability must still be held when the request is processed.

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection no longer holds the controller capability

entry.name: invalid_serial
entry.summary: serial zero is reserved for the initial status

entry.name: identity
entry.summary: identify was sent twice, or after start

event.name: created

description.summary: the server-assigned nonzero run epoch

event.description: The epoch combines epoch_hi as the upper 32 bits and epoch_lo as the lower 32 bits. It is unique within this server's lifetime; a client must also bind its handles to the identity of the live compositor and this connection. available is zero in version 1: discovery does not promise operations that the implementation cannot enforce yet.

event.name: status

description.summary: status without desktop content

event.description: Sent initially with serial zero, then in answer to a successful query. Version 1 is always inactive.

request.name: start

description.summary: ask for control of one output

request.description: Capabilities are explicit, nonempty and limited to this version's capability bits. Before version 5 only one run may await consent or be active at a time, and a request beside another is refused with busy. From version 5 runs are independent: several may be active at once, each holding its own keys and buttons, and a run that must ask the person waits in the awaiting_consent phase until the runs asked before it are answered. No desktop content is sent before consent. Serial must be nonzero. From version 4 a run must be identified first (unidentified otherwise). Observe, semantic, pointer and keyboard need the app's desktop-control service, capture its screen-capture service. A service the person turned off for the app refuses the request with denied. When every needed service is allowed the run is active before completed; otherwise the session authority asks the person and the run awaits consent. A version 2 or 3 run is asked every time and its answer is not remembered. A run that was revoked stays revoked: start on its session is refused with stale_epoch (busy from older servers), and a client destroys the session and gets another for a fresh run. denied comes before stale_epoch and busy.

request.name: button

description.summary: press or release a pointer button where the pointer is

request.description: The release of a button this run holds needs only the grant: it is delivered whatever revision it carries and wherever the pointer is, since the press may itself have changed the layout.

request.name: key

description.summary: deliver a Linux evdev key through the normal keyboard router

request.description: The server owns held state and timestamps. Reserved session and power actions are not available. The release of a key this run holds needs only the grant, whatever revision it carries and wherever the keyboard focus went.

description.summary: revoke this run; cleanup is safe to repeat

request.name: resume

description.summary: continue a suspended run

request.description: A run suspended while an authentication prompt or a protected session panel held the keyboard resumes by itself when it closes. This request resumes it at once when nothing blocks it any more; it is refused with blocked otherwise. It never asks the person again.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: the granted output's current logical rectangle

event.description: This event is followed by status. It is sent again each time revision advances; input carrying an earlier revision is refused with stale_geometry. A changed rectangle, scale or transform of the output advances revision. While the run observes (version 3 and the observe capability), so does a change in where the windows its observations list lie on this output: a window's origin, size or scale, a window appearing in or leaving that list, or a change in their stacking order. A changed title, focus, app id or published snapshot leaves revision as it is and is announced by semantic_changed alone. Capture uses the same output, upright in buffer pixels.

description.summary: the request was dispatched, not proof that the application acted

request.name: observe

description.summary: a complete consented observation with authoritative window transforms

request.description: Includes third-party window metadata without claiming semantic support. Native snapshots are surface-owned, bounded and versioned. Protected session and authentication surfaces are excluded.

request.name: perform

description.summary: route one supported action to its exact publication revision

request.description: Requires observe and semantic consent. Payload is a sealed bounded Invocation. Completion reports the native runtime's result; applications may finish after a timeout, so uncertain outcomes must not be replayed.

request.name: identify

description.summary: name the process the run is for

request.description: The controller names the local process it serves: its process id and its start time in clock ticks since boot (field 22 of /proc/PID/stat), start_hi holding the upper 32 bits. Sent at most once, before start. The compositor checks that the process still has that start time, then finds its app: the nearest ancestor that is a connected application client whose windows name one desktop entry, else the executable of the process's parent. A process it cannot name makes start refuse with unidentified. On a run that already ended, as when the session locked, it is ignored.

request.name: select_capture

description.summary: make the next output capture source this run's

request.description: The next ext_output_image_capture_source_v1 this connection creates belongs to this run: it captures only while this run is active with the capture capability on that output, and stops with this run alone. A later select_capture on any session of the connection replaces the selection. Without a selection a source belongs to the first run of the connection that may capture that output.

interface.name: cupertino_control_authority_v1

description.summary: the supervised session agent's consent authority

interface.description: Offered only to the session-lock role. One authority may be bound at once. Its loss revokes the runs awaiting its answer; a run an app's remembered answers started needs no authority. Consent must name a registered surface and a fresh physical input serial delivered to that surface. The controller cannot bind this interface or approve its own request. Requests come one at a time: the next requested event follows only once the earlier request was answered or ended.

request.name: answer

description.summary: the person's answer to a request

request.description: allow 1 approves the run and, from version 2, remembers allow for each asked service of its app. allow 2 (version 2) refuses the run and remembers deny for each asked service. Both need a fresh physical input serial on the registered surface; a deny without one refuses this run only. allow 0 refuses this run only and remembers nothing (the panel was dismissed or could not be shown).

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: identity is a desktop entry id

entry.name: executable
entry.summary: identity is an absolute executable path

event.name: app

description.summary: the app the next requested event asks for

event.description: Sent right before requested for a run that names its app. name is the desktop entry's name, or the executable's file name. services holds the services asked (desktop control 1, screen capture 2), only those the app has no remembered answer for. remembered is 1 when the answer will be remembered for the app, 0 when it applies to this run only.
